meta.title: Nearby Share Alternative That Includes iPhone | BIShare
meta.description: Nearby Share skips the iPhone. BIShare is the cross-platform Nearby Share alternative: send between Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac & Linux — nearby or by link. Free.

hero.title: A Nearby Share alternative for every device
hero.body: Nearby Share — now Quick Share — is quick between Android phones and even reaches Windows, but it stops dead at the iPhone. BIShare picks up where it leaves off: send files between Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac and Linux, instantly over your local Wi-Fi, or with a link the other side opens in any browser. No account, no app on their end.

why.title: Where Nearby Share stops
why.body: Nearby Share pairs beautifully across Android phones, Chromebooks, and — with the Quick Share app — Windows. But it was never built to talk to Apple devices, so sending that same photo to a friend's iPhone drops you back to chat apps that crush the quality or email that caps the size. BIShare closes the gap: one tool that treats Android and iPhone as equals, alongside Windows, Mac, and Linux.

0.b: Pick the device across the room and send. Files travel straight from one device to the other, end-to-end encrypted, never touching a server — and it still works on a phone hotspot with no internet at all.

1.b: Not in the same room? You get a share link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. The other side opens it in any browser and downloads — no install, no sign-up. The link expires on its own after 24 hours.

2.b: One app for Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac, and Linux. Push a file from your Android to a friend's iPhone, or from a Windows PC to a Mac — any device to any device, both directions.

comparison.title: Nearby Share vs AirDrop vs BIShare

0.q: What's the best Nearby Share alternative that works with iPhone?
0.a: BIShare. Nearby Share (Quick Share) covers Android, Chromebooks, and Windows but leaves out Apple devices entirely. BIShare adds the iPhone and Mac to that list, so a single tool moves files between all of them in any direction.

1.q: Can Nearby Share or Quick Share send to an iPhone?
1.a: No. Nearby Share and Quick Share only pair with Android, Chromebooks, and Windows PCs — there is no iPhone or iPad support. To send from an Android phone to an iPhone you need a cross-platform tool like BIShare, which treats both the same.

2.q: How do I send files from Android to iPhone without Nearby Share?
2.a: Install BIShare on the Android phone (the iPhone side doesn't even need the app). On the same Wi-Fi, pick the device and send directly. Apart? Share the link, QR, or 6-character code and the iPhone downloads it in Safari — no App Store trip required.

3.q: Does the other person need to install BIShare?
3.a: Not for a share link. They just open it in any browser and download — no app, no account on their end. Installing the app makes nearby transfers faster and unlocks every feature, but it's never required to receive a file.

4.q: Is BIShare free like Nearby Share?
4.a: Yes — free, with no account. Nearby transfers over your own Wi-Fi have no size caps, and share links work for anyone, on any platform, up to 10 GB per transfer.

cta.title: Send to any device, not just Android
cta.body: Free, no account. Install on Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac, or Linux and start sending — the other side doesn't even need the app.
